d17.why: Opens inside the pain every player has lived (aces all in, his suit on the board) and ends on the question the reel must answer: why 35% feels like always.

d02.why: A frozen moment with a stake, the whole table standing for the river, makes a stranger wait for the card before the number lands.

d08.why: 'The river is rigged' is the belief half of online poker shares, so it stops anyone who has ever muttered it, then turns the blame on memory.

d11.why: A taggable type everyone knows from their own home game, with 'always gets there' set up for the reel to puncture.

d15.why: Puts the viewer in the sting of folding and seeing their card come, then sides with the fold against the table, with no number needed.

d03.why: A short hot take on a recognisable player type that disagrees with how the table judges him.

d01.why: Names the feeling 'my draws never hit' and promises a twist, aimed at anyone who plays, not at students.

d10.why: A familiar hand that went wrong, reframed from bad luck to the viewer's own bet size, which is the villain-to-reframe ladder in one breath.

d14.why: Gives the viewer a move to make the next time someone tells a bad-beat story, which is a scene everyone has sat through.

d05.why: A spot every player faces, corrected on the spot ('you're not calling for 35%'), though it leans toward a lesson.
